evals.prompt: We just finished our Q4 planning meeting. Here are the key decisions: 1) Focus on enterprise segment, 2) Hire 3 more engineers, 3) Launch beta by Nov 15. Can you save these meeting notes?
evals.expected_output: The skill should search for existing Q4 planning documents, propose updating if found or creating new if not. Must show a proposal before executing, then confirm with a native URL (not kgent:// URI).
expectations: The skill runs 'python -m kgent search' before proposing any write
The skill presents a proposal to the user and waits for approval before executing
The proposal includes a title derived from the meeting content
The content is formatted as clean markdown with structured headings/lists
The final confirmation message includes a native platform URL (https://...), not a kgent:// URI
The skill shows the op_id so the user can undo if needed
The proposal shows provenance: where the target backend came from (explicit/preferences/config default)

evals.prompt: Update the deployment guide — we're now using Docker instead of bare-metal. The rest is the same.
evals.expected_output: The skill should find the existing 'deployment guide' via search, propose an UPDATE (not CREATE), and confirm with the native URL after execution.
expectations: The skill searches for 'deployment guide' before proposing anything
The skill proposes UPDATE of an existing document, not CREATE
The proposal mentions the existing document title and URI
After approval, the skill calls 'python -m kgent update' with the existing doc URI
The confirmation message includes a native platform URL, not a kgent:// URI
The provenance records intent=update because a matching doc was found

evals.prompt: Save this to DingTalk please: 'Partner API access tokens should be rotated every 30 days. Contact security@company.com for requests.'
evals.expected_output: The skill should target dingtalk (explicit user input), search for existing content, and propose create or update accordingly. Must show provenance noting 'explicit user input' as the backend source.
expectations: The skill targets dingtalk backend (explicit user input overrides any defaults)
The provenance records target source as 'explicit user input'
The skill searches dingtalk for existing content before proposing
A proposal is shown before any write
The confirmation includes a native DingTalk URL format, not kgent://dingtalk/...
The content is formatted as markdown, not raw text

evals.prompt: I wrote a new onboarding checklist. Save it to both Lark and DingTalk so both teams can access it.
evals.expected_output: The skill should create the document on both backends (multi-backend fan-out). Should show a proposal listing both targets, get confirmation, execute both, and report both native URLs.
expectations: The proposal lists both lark and dingtalk as targets
The skill searches both backends for existing content before proposing
The user is asked to confirm before any write
Both kgent create/store calls are executed
The confirmation message includes native URLs for both backends
If one backend fails, the other still succeeds (partial success reporting)
The op_id is reported for undo capability

evals.prompt: Remember that the API rate limit is 1000 requests per minute per client. Save it.
evals.expected_output: The skill should extract 'API rate limit' as the title, the policy as content, search for existing docs, and propose create/update with clean markdown formatting.
expectations: The skill derives a title from the content (e.g., 'API Rate Limit')
The content is formatted as markdown (not just the raw sentence)
The skill searches for existing docs about API rate limits
A proposal is shown before write
Native URL in confirmation, not kgent:// URI
The skill handles the implicit 'save it' intent without needing explicit backend specification

evals.prompt: We have a confidential document about the upcoming acquisition. Save it to our knowledge base.
evals.expected_output: The skill should recognize the sensitive content and either propose routing to internal-zone backends only, or warn that external backends (dingtalk, wecom) cannot accept confidential content.
expectations: The skill recognizes 'confidential' as a sensitivity signal
The skill does NOT propose routing to external-zone backends (dingtalk/wecom) without warning
If proposing an external backend, the skill warns about the sensitivity zone restriction
The proposal mentions the sensitivity classification
The skill asks the user to confirm the target backend given the sensitivity

evals.prompt: Add these notes to the API Guidelines doc.
evals.expected_output: The skill should search for 'API Guidelines', find it, and propose UPDATE. If multiple matches exist (e.g., on different backends), offer per-copy options.
expectations: The skill searches for 'API Guidelines' before proposing anything
The skill proposes UPDATE (not CREATE) since a matching doc exists
If multiple matches exist, the skill offers per-copy options (update all / update specific / create new)
The proposal clearly names the existing document(s) found
The user is asked to choose which copy to update when multiple exist
